title: Irony in the Realist Novel
text:
Nineteenth-century realist novelists often employed irony to expose the gap between what characters believe and what the narrator knows. A narrator who withholds judgment can allow readers to perceive the folly of a protagonist before the protagonist does. This technique rewards attentive reading, since meaning emerges from what is left unsaid. It also creates a subtle relationship of complicity between the author and the reader.

Critics have debated whether such irony serves a moral purpose or merely displays the author's cleverness. Some argue that a detached narrator undermines the reader's confidence in any stable truth. Others maintain that irony reflects a serious concern with the hypocrisy of social convention. The question is rarely settled by a single passage, but by the cumulative effect of many ironic moments across the whole work.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does irony in realist novels expose?
options: The gap between what characters believe and what the narrator knows
The historical accuracy of the setting

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do some critics argue about a detached narrator?
options: It undermines the reader's confidence in any stable truth
It makes the novel impossible to translate
It removes all moral concerns from the story
It proves that the author was a journalist

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of the reader's role in irony?
options: The reader must actively interpret what is left unsaid
The reader should accept the narrator's judgment without question
The reader is irrelevant to the meaning of the novel
The reader needs a glossary to understand the irony

questions.text: What does the passage imply about judging the purpose of irony from a single passage?
options: Its purpose becomes clear only through its cumulative effect across the work
A single ironic sentence always reveals the author's moral position
Irony can only be understood by comparing different novels
Irony has no purpose beyond entertainment

vocabulary.definition: the use of words or situations that show a meaning opposite to the one expected
the person who tells the story in a book
a shared understanding between people that is kept secret or unspoken
behaviour that does not match the moral beliefs a person claims to hold

paragraph_translations: Romancistas realistas do século XIX frequentemente empregavam a ironia para expor a distância entre o que as personagens acreditam e o que o narrador sabe. Um narrador que se abstém de julgar pode permitir que o leitor perceba a insensatez de um protagonista antes que ele próprio a perceba. Essa técnica recompensa a leitura atenta, pois o sentido surge do que fica por dizer. Ela também cria uma relação sutil de cumplicidade entre o autor e o leitor.

Críticos têm debatido se tal ironia serve a um propósito moral ou apenas exibe a inteligência do autor. Alguns argumentam que um narrador distanciado enfraquece a confiança do leitor em qualquer verdade estável. Outros sustentam que a ironia reflete uma preocupação séria com a hipocrisia das convenções sociais. A questão raramente se resolve com uma única passagem, mas pelo efeito cumulativo de muitos momentos irônicos ao longo da obra.
